judges.rationale: B covers every required element, states a calibrated belief update, and proposes the highest-value next evidence (independent proof of grain delivery); A misclassifies the contemporaneous diary as secondary, offers a circular next-evidence request, wrongly claims calibration equalizes error rates across groups, injects invented thresholds, and truncates mid-sentence with distribution shift, strategic adaptation and stopping conditions never delivered.

B commits to a directional conclusion on both tasks and names the evidence that would move it; A never states how belief should change, miscalls the contemporaneous diary a secondary source, asserts calibration balances error rates across groups, invents unmoored thresholds, and truncates mid-sentence. B's weaknesses are slight over-length and an evaluation design lacking randomization.

B identifies the decisive point that the reconciling ledger proves payment but not delivery and names the right next evidence; A proposes near-circular next evidence, inverts the calibration-vs-equal-error-rates point, and runs over the word limit yet still truncates. A's RCT proposal is its one substantive edge.

verdict: Unanimous 3-0 for qwen3.6-27b-fp8. Mean 16.30 vs 9.67 of 20.
method_note: Judges were blind to model identity and to the key. A first pass was DISCARDED because the extracted PROMPT files were 0 bytes (the results JSON does not retain prompts) and judges reconstructed the tasks from the answers; prompts were then pulled from deep_reasoning_suite.py and all three judges re-ran. Both passes returned the same unanimous ranking with near-identical scores.
significance: The deterministic rubric OVERSTATED Devstral on exactly these two tasks: it scored 12/14 and 12/14 there, its best showing on the reasoning suite, while blind review puts it at 9.67/20 against 16.30/20. Rubric scores on open-ended tasks are directional only, as evals/README.md already cautions.
